radiology_report:
Subject: mpMRI Prostate
Date: 15 January 2025
Facility: Amsterdam UMC (VUmc location)

Clinical indication: Evaluation of elevated PSA (17.0 ng/mL) and clinical suspicion of malignancy.

FINDINGS: The gland measures 36.82 mL in total volume. T2-weighted sequences highlight a distinct, 18 mm hypointense focus within the right peripheral zone, spanning the base to mid-gland. Diffusion-weighted imaging reveals pronounced restriction with corresponding ADC hypointensity. Dynamic contrast-enhanced phases demonstrate early, focal arterial enhancement localized to the lesion. There is no evidence of extraprostatic extension, seminal vesicle invasion, or pelvic lymphadenopathy.

IMPRESSION: PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right peripheral zone. Prostate volume 36.82 mL yielding a PSA density of 0.462 ng/mL/mL. csPCa predicted probability 0.85766834

previous_notes.author: Dr. R. van den Berg (GP)
previous_notes.text: The patient was reviewed following a PSA reading of 16.1 ng/mL in May 2024. Symptoms remain minimal with an IPSS score of four, and cross-sectional imaging was arranged to clarify the aetiology of the persistent elevation. A routine urinalysis was unremarkable ahead of the planned urology visit.

previous_notes.author: Dr. R. van den Berg (GP)
previous_notes.text: Follow-up consultation regarding a PSA of 15.3 ng/mL obtained in September 2023. The gentleman reports only mild voiding frequency without nocturia or urgency, and a repeat PSA was arranged to monitor the trajectory.
